cards.text: After this, Jesus heads out into the Judean countryside with His disciples. He spends some time with them there. And He baptizes.
Meanwhile John, who's been baptizing people with water out beyond the Jordan (John 1:26, 28), is baptizing at Aenon near Salim. And people KEEP coming.

cards.question: Why is John baptizing at Aenon near Salim?

answers.text: It is close to the temple
It is near the main road

cards.question: The writer slips in a side note here. At this point, John has already been thrown into prison.

cards.text: Then an argument breaks out between John's disciples and a certain Jew.

cards.question: What's the argument between John's disciples and this man about?

cards.text: So John's disciples go to him and call him Rabbi. They bring up the One who was with John beyond the Jordan, the One John testified about.

cards.question: John's disciples have news about that One, Jesus. What do they tell John?

answers.text: He is baptizing and everyone is going to Him
He has left Judea and gone back to Galilee
He wants John to come and baptize with Him

cards.text: Everybody's going to the new guy? A shiny new stamper once took MY spot on the counter, so I'm leaning WAY in to hear how John answers this one, friend.

cards.question: John answers that a man can receive only what is given him from ___.
John reminds his disciples of something they heard him say themselves. What was it?

answers.text: I am not the Christ but am sent ahead of Him
I am the Christ but must wait for my time
I am sent to baptize until He is ready

cards.text: Then John paints a wedding picture, and now he's speaking MY language. The bride belongs to the bridegroom, and the friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him.

cards.question: In John's wedding picture, how does the friend of the bridegroom feel when he hears the bridegroom's voice?
John says that joy of the bridegroom's friend is his own joy, and it is now complete.
So John sums up where he stands next to Jesus: He must ___; I must ___.

cards.text: John keeps going. He talks about two kinds of speakers: the One who comes from above, and the one who is from the earth.

cards.question: John says the one from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks like it. What does he say about the One who comes from heaven?

cards.text: The One from heaven testifies to what He has seen and heard. That's not something He picked up secondhand in a group chat. That's an EYEWITNESS.

cards.question: John says everyone accepts the testimony of the One from heaven.
John adds a line about whoever does accept His testimony. What has that person certified?

answers.text: That he has kept the law
That he is ready to be baptized

cards.text: Why do His words carry so much weight? Because the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God.

cards.question: John says God gives the Spirit without ___.
John says the Father loves the Son but has placed only some things in His hands.

cards.text: Then John lands the whole thing with two roads: believe in the Son, or reject Him. No third lane, friend. Not even a shoulder to pull over on.

cards.question: What does whoever believes in the Son have?
John says whoever rejects the Son will not see life, and the wrath of God remains on him.

findings.problem: The passage opens with "After this," but the opening card never says what "this" is. The verse follows Jesus' talk with Nicodemus (John 3:1-21), and without that, the baker gets no context for where the passage starts.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says Jesus is in the Judean countryside and that He baptizes. That gives away half of the right answer ("He is baptizing") and rules out the wrong answer "He has left Judea and gone back to Galilee."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites John 3:27 but tells nothing from that verse. It only reacts to John 3:26 ("everyone is going to Him"). The citation doesn't match what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke and a reaction. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride along on a card that tells part of the passage, for example by setting up John's reply in 3:27.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "I am sent to baptize until He is ready" is close in meaning to the right answer ("sent ahead of Him"). It also echoes John 1:33 ("the One who sent me to baptize with water"), so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke puts Jesus, the One from heaven, inside the modern image ("picked up secondhand in a group chat"). That blends the comparison with the Bible setting, and it makes Jesus the subject of the joke.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.
